content.text:
## Summary

**Defect found:** The form's `Full name`, `Email address`, `Password`, and `How did you hear about us?` fields used plain `<div class="field-label">` elements for their captions instead of real `<label>` elements. Nothing programmatically associated the visible text with its `<input>`/`<select>`, so screen reader users got no accessible name for any field (WCAG 1.3.1, 4.1.2, 3.3.2 failures) — even though the fields themselves were already native and keyboard-operable.

**Fixes applied (all in `index.html`):**
1. Converted each `.field-label` div into a `<label>` tied to its control via matching `id`/`for` pairs (`full-name`, `email`, `password`, `hear-about`).
2. Added `display: block` to the `.field-label` CSS rule, since `<label>` is inline by default and `<div>` was block — this keeps the visual layout pixel-identical to before.
3. Added `name` and `autocomplete` attributes (`name`, `email`, `new-password`) on the three text inputs to satisfy WCAG 1.3.5 (Identify Input Purpose), which is free functionality browsers already expect for signup forms.

**Left alone (already compliant):**
- All controls are native `input`, `select`, and `button` elements, so keyboard focus order, Tab/Shift+Tab navigation, Enter/Space activation, and native focus indicators (no `outline` was suppressed anywhere in the CSS) already work correctly — no custom widget behavior to reimplement.
- The `data-track="submit"` attribute, the `signup-form` submit handler, and the `window.__activated` instrumentation script are untouched.
- Text/background color combinations (button, `.fine`, `.lead`) were checked and all exceed the 4.5:1 AA contrast ratio for normal text, so no color changes were needed.
- No other landmarks, headings, or interactive elements were missing accessible names.

The page now has properly labeled form controls while preserving the exact same visual design and mouse/keyboard behavior.
